items: Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Iran says Hormuz stays shut and there are no nuclear talks until the US meets its demands, as one report says US strikes could come as early as 4 November → the risk of a wider war after the midterms keeps oil, shipping and regional risk premiums high as the EGX reopens.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The pound holds at EGP 56.12 per dollar at the CBE as banks open Sunday at 56.04–56.19 to sell, the first quotes after the hike → the hike has not yet moved the pound, so today's EGX session tests how equities price higher rates.

Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income and the carry trade but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The S&P 500 falls 1.8% and the Nasdaq 2.9% on Friday after Intel's outlook, while gold drops 3.52% to $3,879.90 → a risk-off week end and forced selling of metals weigh on sentiment toward emerging markets before the EGX reopens.

Qatari mediators in Tehran deliver a Vance letter proposing a new diplomatic process, with a meeting possible within a week in Doha or Istanbul → talks offer a path away from escalation, but reports say Trump has told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the midterms.

The CBE raises rates by 100 bp to a 20% deposit rate after Thursday's close, its first hike since March 2024, against a Reuters poll that expected a hold → the pound near record lows at EGP 56.12 and heavy foreign selling of local debt push the CBE to defend the carry trade; Sunday is the EGX's first session to price it.

EGX30 rises 0.64% to 49,596.14 on Thursday as Banque du Caire's EGP 36.37 bn offering executes and lifts turnover to EGP 43.9 bn → foreign institutions net buy EGP 29.2 bn, mostly through the bank's offering, while 180 stocks rise and 31 fall before trading in BQDC starts on 2 November.

The IMF targets a staff-level deal on Egypt's final review before mid-December, worth about $2.3 bn in final disbursements → Kozack says talks focus on tight monetary policy, which the CBE's hike now delivers.

Brent rises 1.04% to $116.08 in early Friday trade after settling at $114.88 on Thursday, as a tanker is hit in Hormuz and US strike talk returns → oil near $116 widens Egypt's fuel import bill while pump prices stay frozen.

The ECB and the Bank of Japan both hold, the BoJ at 1.25% by 8-1, while Reuters sources call a 17 December ECB hike all but certain → global policy stays tight after US growth beats forecasts at 3.4%, limiting appetite for emerging-market debt.

The CBE raises rates by 100 bp to a 20% deposit rate, its first hike since March 2024, when most analysts expected a hold → the pound's slide past 56 and about $1.67 bn of foreign and Arab debt selling in three days (derived) push the CBE to defend the carry trade.

The Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack voting for a hike, and markets largely price a December hike → elevated inflation and war-driven uncertainty keep US yields high (10-year 5.04%), narrowing the carry that holds foreign money in Egyptian bills.

EGX30 closes Thursday 0.64% higher at 49,596.14 while the EGX70 jumps 2.77% → local buyers absorb foreign selling (foreign institutions net sell EGP 229.1 mn on Wednesday), leaving the index about 2.85% lower over five sessions (derived).
Foreign and Arab net selling of Egyptian bills and bonds slows to $391 mn on Wednesday from $619.1 mn → debt outflows continue but ease as the pound holds at EGP 56.20 at the CBE.

Banque du Caire's retail book closes 27 times covered and the sale is upsized to 45%, with trading expected on 2 November → EGP 49.2 bn of retail orders chase EGP 1.8 bn of stock, showing local appetite for quality state assets even in a falling market.

EGP passes 56 per dollar at the CBE (sell 56.3511 on Monday) as foreign and Arab investors net sell about $664 mn of bills and bonds → secondary-market debt selling and regional risk drive the slide; importers lose, USD earners gain, and Thursday's CBE meeting is the test.

EGX30 closes Monday at 48,416.94, down 8.4% in three sessions, and the FRA halves brokers' minimum liquid capital ratio to 5% → foreign selling and forced selling by leveraged holders prompt the regulator to ease the rule through Thursday.

Brent trades near $116 on Tuesday morning, about 55% above the $75 in Egypt's budget (derived) → Hormuz flows run at about 60% of normal and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia add supply fear, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Egypt's parliament backs military support for Saudi Arabia while the Houthis keep firing at Riyadh and the Eastern Province → a closer link to the regional war lifts Egypt's risk premium and puts Suez and tourism sentiment at risk.

The Fed decides today with a hold priced at about 93% after September's hike to 3.75–4.00% → a firm Fed keeps foreign holders of Egyptian bills under pressure and leaves the CBE no room to cut on Thursday.

stories.h: EGX30 falls 1.72% in the first session after the rate hike as developers lead losses
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; See News; Youm7; Al Mal; EnterpriseAM
stories.what: The EGX30 closes Sunday at 48,744.01, down 1.72%; the EGX70 falls 0.68% and the EGX100 1.01%. 148 stocks fall and 63 rise on turnover of about EGP 7.2 bn, 35% below the 90-day average. Palm Hills (-7.0%), GB Corp (-6.9%) and Ibnsina Pharma (-4.9%) lead losses among large names, while ADIB (+3.4%), AMOC (+2.2%) and Edita (+1.6%) gain. Foreigners net sell EGP 40.6 mn and Arabs EGP 89.5 mn, while Egyptians net buy EGP 130.2 mn.
stories.why: It is the first session after the CBE's 100 bp hike; developers and consumer lenders, which depend on credit, fall most. None of the sources gives a single cause.
stories.aff: Developers, consumer finance, foreign-held blue chips and retail investors, who make up 79% of trading.
stories.eg: EnterpriseAM puts the EGX30 up 16.5% year to date after the drop.
stories.egx: Bearish for developers and NBFIs; banks and AMOC hold up.
stories.names: Palm Hills, GB Corp, Ibnsina, U Consumer Finance (down); ADIB, AMOC, Edita (up).

key.l: Banque du Caire private-placement orders, an EGX record

stories.h: Banque du Caire debuts today as BQDC after a record private book
stories.what: Banque du Caire starts trading today as BQDC, the state's first IPO since United Bank in December 2024. The 45% stake sold at EGP 5.30, the top of the EGP 4.82–5.30 range, raising EGP 36.37 bn and valuing the bank at EGP 80.83 bn. The private tranche drew EGP 205.8 bn of orders, the most an EGX placement has recorded, and the EBRD and IFC each committed $100 mn as cornerstones.
stories.why: Banque Misr sells part of its stake under the state ownership programme and keeps 55% under a lock-up, EnterpriseAM says.
stories.aff: Brokerages, sentiment toward state-bank listings and the privatisation programme.
stories.eg: Adviser Baker Tilly puts fair value at the offer price, while two brokerages put it at EGP 6.55 and EGP 7.80.
stories.egx: Bullish for brokers and sentiment if the stock holds above EGP 5.30; CI Capital can buy back retail shares at that price for 30 days.

key.l: extra yearly cost of the hike, per a finance official

stories.h: State refinances EGP 4.3 tn in four months as the hike adds EGP 150 bn to the bill
stories.what: The finance ministry borrows about EGP 4.3 tn at home from July to October, almost all to refinance maturing debt, against a full-year plan of EGP 3.4 tn in new debt. Bills make up 85% of domestic issuance and new debt matures in about a year on average. A senior official puts the extra cost of the 100 bp hike at EGP 150 bn. The first auction after the hike sells 364-day bills at 26.076% and takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target.
stories.why: Short maturities mean the hike passes into the interest bill quickly; domestic debt stands at EGP 13.68 tn.
stories.aff: The budget deficit, bank income from bills and the state's room to spend.
stories.eg: Foreign holdings of local government debt fell to $27.1 bn in March from $38.1 bn in January, EnterpriseAM says.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks' bill income; bearish for the fiscal outlook and for sectors that rely on state spending.

key.l: minimum dollar transfer to reserve NUCA land

stories.h: NUCA lets companies paying in dollars from abroad skip land bidding
stories.what: From November, Egyptian and foreign companies that pay the full price of NUCA land in dollars wired from abroad get priority and skip price bidding. They must wire at least $100k to reserve and pay in full within a month or forfeit the deposit; some plots will be sold only for dollars. Separately, ACUD is drafting deadline extensions for developers in the New Capital as costs and interest rates climb.
stories.why: The state wants foreign currency; net foreign investment in Egyptian property reached $2.8 bn in FY 2025/26, up 47%.
stories.aff: Developers with foreign partners or dollar income, land prices and FX inflows.
stories.eg: A new route for dollar inflows while foreign money leaves local debt.
stories.egx: Mixed for developers: dollar buyers gain priority, but higher rates weigh on the sector.

stories.h: Brent drops about 3% as Iran floats a two-day Hormuz plan and OPEC+ holds output
stories.src: Reuters via FinanceFeeds; The National; CNBC
stories.what: Brent's January contract falls $3.37 to about $109.75 by 04:07 GMT on Monday, down 3.2% from Friday's $113.43 settlement; the expired December contract settled at $117.64. On Sunday, seven OPEC+ members keep December targets unchanged at about 31 mn bpd and set the next meeting for 29 November.
stories.why: Iran says a Qatari-brokered plan could partly reopen Hormuz within two days, which takes some risk premium out of prices; most Gulf producers already pump below their targets.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill, the pound and inflation expectations.
stories.eg: A lower oil price eases pressure on the import bill if the plan holds.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for importers and energy users; less supportive for oil-linked AMOC.

key.l: Iran's new timeline to partly reopen Hormuz

stories.h: Iran shortens its Hormuz plan to two days while Trump keeps strikes on the table
stories.what: Two days of Qatar-mediated talks open a possible path to a deal, and Iran shortens the wait before a partial reopening of Hormuz from seven days to two. Iran's conditions include lifting the US naval blockade, oil sanctions waivers and unfrozen assets. Trump says talks are going fine but says the US still has one or two nuclear sites to deal with, and at least four tankers are hit on Friday and Saturday.
stories.why: Both sides keep diplomacy and escalation open ahead of the US midterms on 3 November.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping, regional risk premiums and Suez traffic.
stories.eg: A reopening would ease Egypt's energy costs; escalation would raise them and delay any Suez recovery.
stories.egx: Neutral: the outcome swings oil, the pound and tourism sentiment this week.

stories.h: AMOC's quarterly profit jumps 154% to EGP 3.475 bn
stories.what: Alexandria Mineral Oils reports sales up 41% to EGP 43.2 bn and net profit up 154% to EGP 3.475 bn for the quarter to 30 September, Youm7 reports. The stock rises 2.21% to EGP 14.31 on Sunday, after 4.87% on Thursday. Misr Chemical Industries also reports profit up 35% to EGP 182.1 mn.
stories.why: Higher oil prices lift the value of refined products; the company's statement on drivers is not in the source.
stories.aff: AMOC shareholders and the energy sector's weight in the index.
stories.eg: Refiners gain while high oil prices hurt most of the economy.
